data.title: ADS: Buy Rating Maintained as Margin Strength and Growth Opportunities Support $175 Price Target
data.description:
Analyst James Ko from Jefferies maintained a Buy rating on Advanced Drainage Systems and keeping the price target at $175.00.

James Ko has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including ADS’s ability to outgrow weak markets through conversion gains, Infiltrator, and expanding water-quality offerings. Residential demand remains soft, but stronger nonresidential activity in data centers, warehouses, and commercial projects provides support. The company’s scale may also help it gain share as smaller competitors face higher material and freight costs.

ADS delivered a record 34.1% first-half adjusted EBITDA margin, demonstrating that pricing and mix are offsetting inflation better than expected. Ko sees a path toward mid-30s margins as volumes recover and resin costs ease, despite near-term freight risks. The StormTrap acquisition adds a growing, asset-light business with cross-selling potential, while valuation near 10x FY2028E EV/EBITDA appears attractive; the price target remains unchanged at $175.

According to TipRanks, Ko is an analyst with an average return of -1.9% and a 25.00% success rate.

In another report released on November 6, KeyBanc also reiterated a Buy rating on the stock with a $185.00 price target.

data.title: SMC Hold: Strong Operating Performance Offset by Limited Near-Term Upside
data.description:
Analyst Lisa Jiang of Morgan Stanley maintained a Hold rating on SMC (OR), with a price target of Yen86,000.00.

Lisa Jiang’s rating is based on a balance between strong operating performance and limited near-term surprise. Second-quarter operating profit exceeded both Morgan Stanley’s estimate and consensus, while the higher full-year forecast suggested earnings momentum and possible upside. However, the result appeared broadly consistent with market expectations, reducing the likelihood of a significant positive reassessment.
Management also announced a buyback that lifted the projected total shareholder return, which could support the stock. At the same time, SMC expects some moderation in sales and profit during the second half and faces uncertainty over the timing of higher labor costs and expanded sales staffing. These offsetting factors make the risk-reward profile balanced, supporting a Hold rather than a more bullish recommendation.

data.title: Banca IFIS: Hold Maintained as NPL Disposal Prospects Offset by Profitability Concerns and Lowered Price Target
data.description:
Intesa Sanpaolo analyst Manuela Meroni maintained a Hold rating on Banca Ifis SPA yesterday and set a price target of €13.70.

Manuela Meroni’s rating is based on several factors, including the prospective sale of Banca IFIS’s non-performing-loan portfolio, which could improve capital strength, support regulatory compliance and allow a renewed focus on corporate lending and shareholder distributions. However, the final economics remain uncertain until binding offers and Bank of Italy requirements are known, while the business outside NPLs continues to show weak underlying profitability.

The expected capital benefit from removing NPLs is encouraging, but it does not resolve the longer-term challenge of improving returns, particularly at illimity, and management does not expect a dividend from 2026 earnings. With 2027–28 earnings estimates reduced by 2% and the price target trimmed from EUR 13.9 to EUR 13.7, Meroni retained a Hold stance until the disposal and profitability recovery provide greater visibility.
